comment:
Read at commit 690ed35, 'chore: bump version to 2.0.1 for library resubmission'. The installed plugin.json is byte-identical to that commit's, and the repository has 606 commits all carrying 2.0.1 after it. Two things settled which one shipped: from 299e77c onwards plugin.json registers a second module, ForgeAnalogVCO, which the installed manifest does not list, and the installed build has no VCO in it at all. Between 690ed35 and 299e77c nothing touches src/AnalogLFO.cpp, its dsp headers or res/AnalogLFO.svg, so every 2.0.1 candidate is the same LFO and 690ed35 is the earliest of them.

The DSP is written out in full in src/dsp/ (LfoCore, DriftEngine, ClockTracker, Waveshape, Swing) and nothing is vendored. Every figure above is from those files.

Index order is not panel order here. Input 1 is Drift CV and input 2 is Character CV, while the panel prints CHAR in the third column and DRIFT in the fourth, so the two are crossed relative to the enum. The tags follow the census positions: Character CV (input 2) sits at x 54.8 under CHAR, Drift CV (input 1) at x 86.9 under DRIFT.

Two places where the maker's own docs do not match the code:
- docs/engine-concept.md and docs/panel.md say the five morph shapes take 'roughly 20% each' and that 80-100% is narrow pulse. src/dsp/Waveshape.hpp:165-185 multiplies morph by 4, giving four crossfade segments of 25%: sine at 0, triangle at 25%, saw at 50%, square at 75% and pulse only at 100%, with the top quarter narrowing the duty from 50% to 5% rather than crossfading.
- docs/io-reference.md says the Phase Offset CV is 'active only when patched'. That is true, and it also means the Phase-Offset trim does nothing while that jack is empty, which nothing in the docs says.

The drift offset is added after the anti-click crossfade (src/dsp/LfoCore.hpp:236), so with DRIFT raised the output can sit a little outside ±5V. The docs describe the output as bipolar ±5V without the qualification.

Swing is gated on clocked mode in two places (src/dsp/Swing.hpp:34 and the display gate at src/AnalogLFO.cpp:344), so the menu setting is stored but inert while free-running, and the on-screen swing overlay is hidden at Straight.

The waveform display is a TransparentWidget with no ParamWidget behind it and no census position, so no click reaches it.

Each instance draws its own random spread coefficients at construction (src/AnalogLFO.cpp:226-234) and saves them in the patch, so two copies of the module are very slightly differently detuned and each one reloads with the character it had.
